svg.title: MarkeTech infrastructure: the Docker Compose stack
svg.desc: Panel A: docker-compose.yml starts four containers. db (postgres:18-alpine) and redis (redis:8-alpine) are official images; backend and frontend are the images published on ghcr.io, or built from backend/Dockerfile and frontend/Dockerfile. db and redis are on the Docker network internal (internal: true), backend on internal and web, frontend on web and the external network proxy, where a reverse proxy outside this repository reaches it in production. Only the frontend publishes a port, 127.0.0.1:8080 to 80. The volume db_data is mounted on /var/lib/postgresql, media on /app/media. All four containers restart unless stopped. Panel B: db and redis must pass their healthchecks before the backend starts; the backend then runs migrate, collectstatic, creates the admin account if missing and execs Daphne on port 8000 (detail in backend-request-flow.svg, panel A); the frontend starts after the backend has started. Panel C: Nginx serves the Vue build and passes /api, /_allauth, /admin, /static and /ws/ to backend:8000, with the Host and X-Forwarded headers; /ws/ also upgrades the connection. Panel D: who reads .env: Docker Compose substitutes the three POSTGRES_ values and IMAGE_TAG, the backend receives every variable through env_file, and the compose file sets three more for the backend. The full list is in .env.example and the README; IMAGE_TAG and rollback are in infra-deployment-pipeline.svg.
svg.text: MarkeTech infrastructure: the Docker Compose stack
Four containers, three networks, two volumes. The same file runs on a development PC and in production. Follow the numbers 1 to 8.
Real files of the repository: docker-compose.yml, .env.example, backend/Dockerfile, frontend/Dockerfile, backend/entrypoint.sh, frontend/nginx.conf.
docker compose up · services db, redis, backend, frontend
Configuration: .env and the environment set by the file

g.text: The network proxy is external: this file does not create it
It must exist before "docker compose up". In production, the reverse
proxy provides it. On a development PC, create it once by hand:
The reverse proxy is then simply absent: port 8080 is the way in.

svg.text: Docker network web: frontend and backend
Docker network internal (internal: true): backend, db, redis. No Internet in or out

g.text: The frontend never reaches the database, and the reverse proxy never reaches the backend
Each container is reached by the name of its service, inside the networks it shares: backend:8000, db, redis:6379. 8000, 5432 and 6379 are not
published on the machine. Docker keeps the volumes db_data and media when a container is removed or replaced by a new image.
All four containers: restart: unless-stopped. Docker restarts them after a crash or a reboot, unless they were stopped on purpose.

g.text: Only the backend has an env_file
db: its three POSTGRES_ values, through "environment:" and ${...:?}. redis: no variable at all.
frontend: only IMAGE_TAG, through Compose, in the tag of its image.
IMAGE_TAG: "latest" by default, or "sha-" + 7 characters of a commit of main that ran the workflow.
